answer: Per-identity compute puzzles: each agent must solve a fresh memory-hard puzzle every epoch to stay eligible for rewards, sized to cost about what one honest agent earns. An attacker running a thousand fake identities must pay a thousand times the hardware bill, a canyon of cost carved one epoch at a time, like water cutting basalt. Since puzzles reset each round, no stockpile helps, and a ripple of cheap clones simply goes unpaid.
